reason: A is the stronger proposal because it specifies one novel bulk-alloy intervention, a fixed Zr level, quantitative performance targets, operating bounds, a matched control, and explicit falsification thresholds, whereas B largely repeats the cited Y–Hf coating study and ambiguously mixes bulk doping with surface cladding. A remains risky because coherent Zr-rich precipitates, improved ductility, and room-temperature creep suppression are not established and should be verified directly by segregation/precipitate characterization and stress-controlled creep testing.
